question: Should authorized `elevated=full` execution bypass configured exec STOP rules?
rationale: Both choices define a consequential security boundary: preserving the established break-glass contract permits intentional bypass, while enforcing STOP rules unconditionally changes elevated-full semantics.

options.title: Retain break-glass bypass
options.body: Keep elevated-full as an explicit bypass, document that STOP rules do not constrain it, and require current-head proof of both ordinary enforcement and elevated bypass behavior.

options.title: Enforce STOP rules universally
options.body: Make denylist matches require approval even under elevated-full and update tests, documentation, and upgrade guidance to reflect the stricter contract.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer landing until a broader exec-policy design establishes whether any configured guardrail may override elevated-full.

recommendation.title: Retain break-glass bypass
recommendation.body: Keep elevated-full as an explicit bypass, document that STOP rules do not constrain it, and require current-head proof of both ordinary enforcement and elevated bypass behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent exec-approval security and node-execution work makes this person the strongest available owner for the break-glass policy decision.
